 Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (8-of-13 FGs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 15-110 loss to the Hornets on Saturday.
 Miami trailed by 21 points entering the fourth quarter, but Mitchell fueled a monster comeback, mostly with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the bench. That didn’t result in a win, but it was another strong performance for him. He has been fantastic this year, averaging 17.0 points, 8.7 assists and 2.3 three-pointers per game, all of which would be career bests for him. He has been a bright spot despite a rough start to the year for Miami.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Davion Mitchell produced 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 assists, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 The good news for fantasy managers was that Mitchell recorded a double-double, which included a game-high 10 assists. However, for category-league managers, the six turnovers hurt. Mitchell logged 33 minutes in Wednesday’s opener, with Pelle Larsson (two points, three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block) taking on the playmaking responsibilities when “Off Night” was on the bench. Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo can also initiate the offense, and they’ll likely need to because Miami lacks depth at point guard. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 BKN 
 Forward 
 #17 
 Davion Mitchell had 13 Points, (4-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, two steals and a 3-pointer on Wednesday. 
 Davion showed how much of a pest he is defensively in this game with his full court pressure and defensive numbers. He did leave the game temporarily after hitting his head on Day’Ron Sharpe’s knee, but he returned to the game. He should be primed to at worst, be a steals and assists streamer for redraft leagues. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Davion Mitchell notched three points (1-of-5 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s exhibition against the Raptors. 
 Like the other Heat starters, Mitchell was shut down at the half. He didn’t have a great night shooting, but that shouldn’t dissuade fantasy managers from selecting “Off Night” in drafts. Miami lacks depth at point guard, especially with Dru Smith (hamstring) not guaranteed to be fully ready when the regular season begins. With Giannis Antetokounmpo joining the lineup, Mitchell could potentially provide more value in assists and three-pointers than he did in 2025-26. 
 Dru Smith 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #12 
 According to Ira Winderman of the Sun-Sentinel, Dru Smith (calf) is out for “a couple of weeks.” 
 Smith, who played a career-high 70 games last season, is dealing with a strained right calf. With the reported timeline, he may be limited when the regular season begins. Smith’s absence doesn’t affect fantasy basketball, but it does leave a Heat team already light on options at point guard down a rotation piece. Starter Davion Mitchell has become more important, especially if Smith isn’t ready when the regular season begins. 
 Kasparas Jakučionis 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 The Athletic’s Sam Amick reports the Bucks pushed for Kasparas Jakučionis to be included in the trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo. 
 Amick, citing league sources, reports the Heat initially attempted to include Davion Mitchell in the trade rather than Jakučionis. With Mitchell on an expiring contract, the Bucks wanted a player with more time remaining on their rookie contract. It was a reasonable ask considering two of the other players the Bucks acquired (Tyler Herro and Jaimie Jaquez Jr.) are also on expiring deals. The Bucks held out and landed Jakučionis, who has three years left on his contract. He remains an intriguing dynasty asset on the rebuilding Bucks. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #45 
 Davion Mitchell amassed 28 points (12-of-24 FGs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets. 
 Mitchell logged a game-high 48 minutes on Tuesday and did just about everything the Heat could have hoped for. He shot the ball well en route to leading the team in scoring, was one of Miami’s top facilitators, and was the Heat’s only player with at least one block and steal apiece. Unfortunately for Mitchell, his blocked game-winning layup attempt will be the lasting memory of what was a very strong performance. Mitchell played 70 games this season and made a big step as a passer. Yet he wasn’t a reliable option when it came to fantasy basketball. 
 Andrew Wiggins 
 MIA 
 Forward 
 #22 
 Andrew Wiggins totaled 27 points (10-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in the loss to the Hornets on Friday. 
 Wiggins was one of several Heat players to make positive contributions on the offensive end of the floor. His 27 points trailed only Davion Mitchell’s 28, as the veteran forward had production across all three scoring levels. Wiggins was also one of the Heat’s best rebounders on the night during his 42 minutes of game action. He finished the season as a fairly comparable fantasy basketball performer as he was a season ago, albeit on fewer points per game. If Wiggins remains on the Heat going forward, he could be in for a similar season.

 Tyler Herro (foot) and Davion Mitchell (shoulder) are available for Sunday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Herro and Mitchell are available for Sunday’s regular-season finale after not playing in Friday’s win over the Wizards. Their returns will push Simone Fontecchio and Kasparas Jakučionis to the bench, with the former offering a higher ceiling when used in a reserve role. A win over the Hawks, combined with a Hornets loss to the Knicks, would move Miami into the No. 9 seed. They would host the 9 vs. 10 game on Wednesday night.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 29 points (12-of-23 FGs, 3-of-7 FTs), 15 rebounds, 11 assists, one block, two three-pointers and five turnovers in a 113-109 loss to the Mavericks on Monday.
 Giannis dominated this game early on and nearly had a triple-double before halftime, and he was able to secure his first one with the Heat just a few minutes into the third quarter. However, it wasn’t enough to get their first win of the season. Giannis was much better than he was in Saturday’s loss to Charlotte, but he didn’t get much help from his co-star Bam Adebayo, who was held to just eight points. Antetokounmpo should continue to post gaudy stat lines, and they’ll head to Atlanta for their next game on Wednesday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Walter Clayton Jr. provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (6-of-7 FGs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and two three-pointers on Monday against the Heat.
 Sergio de Larrea had been playing well off the bench for Dallas, but he exited early from this game with a knee injury.  Tyler Herro tallied 23 points (7-of-14 FGs, 6-of-10 FTs), 10 rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pacers.
 Herro has now scored 23 points or more in three of his first four games with the Bucks, with Saturday’s loss to the 76ers being the exception. The performance against the Pacers may have been his best, as Herro finished three assists shy of a triple-double and recorded a complete stat line. The preseason perimeter rotation concerns seem to have taken care of themselves, as the Bucks waived Kevin Porter Jr. before the season started, and neither Caris LeVert nor Gary Trent Jr. has appeared in a game. That’s good news for those rostering Herro, as he could be in for a big season.

 Ryan Rollins accumulated 19 points (7-of-14 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Monday’s win over the Pacers.
 Rollins got off to a relatively slow start, averaging 11.7 points and shooting 35.1 percent from the field in Milwaukee’s first three games. He was better on Monday, shooting 50 percent from the field and 3-of-7 from beyond the arc. Rollins didn’t record any defensive stats, but fantasy managers should be pleased with the offensive output.

 Washington has been a solid source of offense for Dallas early on this season. This was his second 20-point game of the season, and he has averaged 15.5 points and 2.0 triples per game thus far. He has been a decent source of steals in years past, and he finally got his first two of the season in this game. That number should regulate, allowing him to be a better fantasy producer moving forward.
